To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) randomization analysis can be used to test the equality of growth and response rates in the context of the growth and response curves, and (2) two multiple-comparisons techniques can be used to supplement randomization analysis of the growth and/or response rates in the growth and response curve analysis.

the randomization analysis can be used to compare any two curves, that the randomization test can be approximated using a standard F test, and that the randomization procedure can be extended to control experimentwise or familywise Type I error rates for multiple comparisons.
the two multiple-comparisons methods we developed can be applied to the randomization analysis (i) of a family of contrast curves and (ii) of a family or a single growth curve.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the randomization analysis can be made more powerful and more efficient by using multiple comparisons procedures.
the randomization analysis is a powerful tool for the analysis of growth curves and response curves.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the randomization analysis can be extended to include multiple-comparisons tests.
randomization analysis of curves can be made more rigorous by controlling the Type I error rate of the multiple comparison tests.
, when the goal is inference on the mean of a response variable, randomization analysis can be supplemented by multiple-comparison methods.
